title: Build Your First Image Classifier
description: Time to train a real AI model, no coding required! We'll use Google's Teachable Machine.

content.value: Train Your Own AI with Teachable Machine

Google Teachable Machine is a free, friendly website that lets you train an image classifier using just your webcam, no code at all. You'll teach the AI to tell apart different hand signs and faces, and it's the same kind of training real AI teams do.
Open teachablemachine.withgoogle.com in your browser and click 'Get Started', then 'Image Project' → 'Standard image model'.

A class is simply one of the groups you want the AI to tell apart. If you're sorting fruit, your classes might be 'apple' and 'banana'. The AI's whole job is to look at a new image and decide which class it belongs to.
Your Project: A Gesture & Mood Detector
You'll train the AI to recognize four classes:

👍  Thumbs Up
👎  Thumbs Down
😀  Happy Face
😢  Sad Face

Every Teachable Machine project follows the same simple steps that all Machine Learning follows: 1) Collect examples for each class using your webcam. 2) Click 'Train Model' so the AI learns the patterns. 3) Preview it live, show a thumbs up and watch the AI guess!

Step 1: COLLECT  → record ~30 webcam samples per class
Step 2: TRAIN    → click 'Train Model' and wait a few seconds
Step 3: TEST     → show a gesture, watch the confidence bars move

When you test it, the AI doesn't just say one answer, it shows a confidence bar for each class, like 'Thumbs Up: 92%, Happy Face: 6%'. That percentage is how sure it is. AI rarely says 100%; it makes its best guess and tells you how confident it feels, just like you might say 'I'm pretty sure that's a dog'.

If the AI keeps mixing up two classes, that's a clue! Usually it means the examples looked too similar, or there weren't enough of them. This is the exact same problem professionals face, and the fix is the same: collect more, clearer, more varied examples.

More examples = a smarter model! Try collecting samples from different angles and lighting so your AI works in lots of situations. Then test it in a spot it never saw during training and see how it does.
Key Takeaway: You just followed the real AI workflow, collect data, train a model, and test it. That's exactly how professionals build AI, just on a bigger scale!

quiz.question: What tool are we using to build an image classifier without code?
quiz.explain: Teachable Machine lets you train image, sound, and pose models right in the browser, no coding needed.

quiz.question: What are the three main steps to build the model?
options: Collect examples, train the model, test it
quiz.explain: Collect data for each class, train the model so it learns the patterns, then test it live.

quiz.question: How can you make your classifier more accurate?
options: Collect more and more varied examples
quiz.explain: More examples, from different angles and lighting, help the model recognize each class more reliably.

quiz.question: The 'confidence bar' showing 'Thumbs Up: 92%' tells you...
options: How sure the AI is about its guess
How many pixels the photo has
quiz.explain: The percentage is the model's confidence, how sure it is that the image belongs to that class.
